rationale: The previous build failed with a compiler internal error attributed to extreme weights, so this candidate flattens every entry into a narrow 0.40-0.55 band: no dimension is saturated at 0.0/1.0, which avoids pathological pass-selection combinations (e.g., maximal flattening plus maximal bogus-control-flow on the same tiny function) that previously triggered the internal error. The target is a very small Shootout-style numeric program (two functions, ~512 bytes of text, a single hot main loop over integer arrays), so heavy transforms like FLA and BCF carry poor runtime payoff; their SecurityGain stays modest (0.50-0.55) while their RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights sit slightly below 0.5 so the selector only applies them where features strongly favor security. Cheap, low-risk diversifiers — SPLIT and IGV — get a mild DiversityGain edge (0.55) to break static pattern matching at negligible cost, and SUB is kept slightly security-leaning since arithmetic substitution is the cheapest way to obscure the integer-heavy kernels in ary3. CorrectnessRisk is uniformly held at 0.40-0.45 across all passes to suppress risky transform stacking on the single hot function while leaving the selector room to act; overall the table trades a small amount of peak obfuscation strength for build robustness and predictable overhead on a program where runtime cost dominates the utility function.
